title: Minimum speed at C
description: Essential: Student correctly states or uses the condition that at point C, gravity provides the centripetal force, leading to v_C = sqrt(gR).

title: Speed at B from energy
description: Important: Student applies the work-energy theorem between B and C, accounting for the change in gravitational potential energy.

title: Normal force at B
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the supporting force at B using Newton's second law for circular motion: N - mg = m v_B^2 / R.

title: Motor work from energy
description: Important: Student relates the motor's work (Pt) to the kinetic energy at B and the work done against friction on the straight track.

title: Correct numerical results
description: Essential: Student provides the final numerical answers for v_C, N_B, and t with correct units.

title: Energy conservation sign error
description: Pitfall: Student uses an incorrect sign for the gravitational potential energy term when applying work-energy between B and C.

title: Forgetting friction work
description: Pitfall: Student omits the work done against friction (F_f * L) when calculating the minimum motor operating time.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: Student shows unit analysis for at least one key equation, confirming dimensional consistency.
